title: Rate limits are keyed per venue and asset, so each destination holds independent allowance state
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.1.5 defines a Rate Limit ID as "a bytes32 key that uniquely identifies a rate limit," whose purpose is to "maintain independent allowance state for each relevant transaction."

The operational sections show how fine that keying goes. A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.2.1.2 identifies the Aave deposit limit as `LIMIT_AAVE_DEPOSIT` "for the underlying asset, the address of the pool, and the address of the aToken"; A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.3.1.2 keys the Basin deposit limit by asset and Basin contract. The limit is therefore not per action type but per (action, asset, venue) tuple.

The risk property this buys is containment. A single compromised or malfunctioning integration can consume only its own allowance; it cannot drain a shared budget and starve — or endanger — every other position. Governance can also express differentiated appetite per venue without writing new code, since each tuple is just another key.

The trade-off is configuration surface: every new asset or pool needs its own limit provisioned, and an unconfigured key is a distinct operational state from a zero limit. A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.1.2.2 acknowledges exactly this by qualifying a behaviour with "where that rate limit is configured."
description: A Rate Limit ID is a bytes32 key; a deposit limit is identified by the function plus underlying asset, pool address and receipt-token address, containing blast radius to one integration.
